options.B: Two veins and one artery
options.C: Two veins and two arteries

question: What is the main goal of actively managing the third stage of labour?

question: Why is hypertension frequently described as a silent condition?

question: What is a key preventative measure community health nurses should teach families about preparing meat?

question: Which key community figures can nurses partner with to encourage male involvement?

question: Why is mixing a chemical disinfectant to the correct ratio so important?

question: What is a common sign that a female patient has too much androgen in her system?

question: Why is quality checks a must-do when buying drugs for the DRF?

question: What is the main purpose of agricultural subsidies provided by the government?

question: What is the main sign of a structural congenital anomaly?

question: A patient wakes up gasping for air two hours after falling asleep and has to sit by the window to breathe. What is this called?

question: A patient with severe diarrhoea complains of dizziness when standing up quickly. What does this finding suggest?

question: Why is female genital mutilation (FGM) traditionally performed?

options.A: To prevent severe pelvic infections in young girls

question: Why is the male pelvis typically narrower and deeper than the female pelvis?

question: What is the best way for community health nurses to help stop unsafe abortions?

question: Why is health care waste management so important in our hospitals?

options.A: To increase the speed of patient discharge procedures

question: What is your main duty as a nurse when a patient comes in with complications from an illegal abortion?

options.A: Report her to security before starting any fluids

question: A patient is unresponsive, not breathing, and has no pulse after choking. What is your immediate nursing action?

question: What should you do when a patient suddenly falls silent during an emotional discussion?

question: What is the main purpose of medication reconciliation during a patient admission?

options.A: Determining which pharmaceutical company manufactured the prescribed drugs

question: What does it mean when a Drug Revolving Fund is described as 'ring-fenced'?

question: How do thiazide diuretics and loop diuretics differ in how they handle calcium?

question: What is the best way to catch mistakes before starting a new IV infusion?

question: What does a 'free hormone' blood test actually measure?

question: What happens in the body during an episode of obstructive sleep apnea?

question: Which of the following will NOT typically cause prevalence to increase?

question: During a fire, why should you use the back of your hand to feel if a closed door is hot?

question: What is the main goal of laws protecting gender rights in healthcare?

question: What is reminiscence therapy?

question: Why must speculums be either single-use plastic or properly sterilized metal?

question: What is the most crucial piece of advice for a patient sent home with a 14-day course of antibiotics for salpingitis?

options.A: Save half the pills in case the infection returns next month
options.B: Double the dose if you miss a pill during the middle of the week
options.C: Stop taking the medication as soon as your pelvic pain goes away
options.D: Finish every single pill, even if you start feeling completely better

explanation: Feeling better doesn't mean all germs are gone. Stopping early can let tougher bacteria survive and bring the infection right back. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h7)

question: Why are large-bore intravenous lines inserted immediately for a patient with heavy APH?

options.A: To allow rapid fluid replacement and emergency blood transfusion
options.B: To prevent the patient from moving her arms during contractions
options.C: To allow continuous measurement of deep core body temperature
options.D: To make it easier to administer daily oral vitamin supplements

explanation: Large-bore cannulas are necessary to quickly replace lost blood volume and prevent the onset of hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h6)

question: Why are nurses strongly advised NOT to recap used needles?

options.A: It violates hospital rules regarding plastic waste recycling
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of accidental needle stick injuries
options.C: It damages the sharp tip making it useless for the next patient
options.D: It wastes valuable nursing time during busy medication rounds

explanation: Trying to guide a tiny cap back onto a used needle is one of the quickest ways to accidentally poke yourself. Drop it straight into the safety box instead! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h7)

question: How does a local food network protect your neighborhood during a transport strike?

options.A: By increasing the cost of basic food items
options.B: By providing a protective buffer of nearby food sources
options.C: By shutting down local markets immediately
options.D: By depending completely on imported supplies

explanation: Exactly! When long-distance transport is blocked, having food grown right in your backyard or nearby keeps everyone fed. Great thinking! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T030#GNS227_U2_T030_h1)

question: What is the main reason nurses use a partograph during labor?

options.A: To screen for sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To monitor labor progress and detect deviations from normal labor early
options.C: To calculate the exact date of conception
options.D: To test the mother's blood glucose levels

explanation: You'll be seeing a lot of the partograph in the maternity ward! It's our trusty visual chart to track how labor is going and catch any warning signs early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h6)

question: You are about to put an oxygen mask on an anxious patient. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Explain the procedure simply to reduce anxiety and calm the patient
options.B: Tie the mask straps as tightly as possible to prevent removal
options.C: Leave the room immediately and let the patient put the mask on alone
options.D: Administer a strong sedative drug without a doctor's order

explanation: Talking calmly to your patient builds trust, eases their panic, and helps them breathe much easier during the setup. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the main goal of practicing medical asepsis (clean technique) on the ward?

options.A: To sterilize multi-use equipment between patients
options.B: To destroy all bacterial spores on the patient's skin
options.C: To reduce the number of pathogens and stop their spread
options.D: To create a completely germ-free surgical environment

explanation: You got it! Medical asepsis is all about reducing the number of germs and stopping them from traveling around the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why is it so powerful to involve traditional and religious leaders in your public health campaigns?

options.A: They hold high community trust, which greatly boosts local participation
options.B: They possess advanced medical degrees to treat complex diseases
options.C: They provide direct financial funding from international donors
options.D: They legally mandate citizens to buy private health insurance

explanation: People listen to their traditional and religious leaders! When these leaders endorse your immunization or health drive, the whole community is much more likely to show up. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h5)

question: What does 'multi-skilling' mean for a nurse?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.B: Possessing certified competence in various clinical tasks
options.C: Being able to perform minor surgeries without a doctor
options.D: Knowing how to operate heavy hospital machinery only

explanation: Correct! Multi-skilling is all about mastering a variety of practical nursing procedures so you can handle different types of patient care. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why would a nurse check out a patient's home environment before they are discharged?

options.A: To identify physical barriers and fall hazards before discharge
options.B: To determine the financial income of the household members
options.C: To verify if the client owns a television or radio
options.D: To inspect the structural plumbing and electrical wiring

explanation: Safety first! Spotting dangerous things like loose rugs or stairs beforehand helps prevent nasty falls when they finally get home. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h3)

question: If a community health nurse wants to help mothers fight iron-deficiency anemia using local foods, which food group should she focus on?

options.A: Clear fruit juices with added artificial colors
options.B: Highly refined starches and sugary beverages
options.C: Saturated cooking oils and bottled water
options.D: Dark green leafy vegetables and local grains

explanation: You nailed it! Dark green veggies and whole local grains are packed with the iron needed to build strong, healthy red blood cells. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T007#GNS227_U3_T007_h3)

question: Why is it smart for community health nurses to work with local market leaders when promoting food hygiene?

options.A: It stops people from selling food altogether
options.B: It guarantees that the local market will receive government funding
options.C: It helps ensure the hygiene messages are accepted and practiced by vendors
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid visiting the market stalls personally

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Market leaders are respected, so getting them on board makes food vendors much more willing to listen and adopt safe habits. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h6)

question: How does the water seal chamber stop air from rushing back into the patient's chest?

options.A: It uses electronic suction to block all backward movement of gases
options.B: It freezes the tubing shut whenever the patient tries to breathe in
options.C: It creates a chemical barrier that destroys outside bacteria instantly
options.D: It acts as a one-way valve that lets air out but not back in

explanation: Think of it like a one-way street! Air bubbles out when the patient breathes out, but the water blocks outside air from getting back in. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h1)
